Deep research agents answer complex ques-
tions through repeated search. They rely on
a harness that runs their tool calls and re-
turns evidence to their context. This cre-
ates a trade-off: Search works best over long
passages, which give enough context for re-
liable semantic matching. But the returned
evidence should be short, because every ob-
servation stays in the agent's context for the
rest of the trajectory. We introduceCORE, a
training-free harness that combines coarse-to-
fine search with context management. CORE
retrieves passages with a dense retriever. It
then reuses the token-level similarities from
a late-interaction reranker to return only the
most relevant snippet from each passage. Con-
text management lets the agent expand the con-
text around sources it has already retrieved and
suppresses repeated snippets. In controlled
closed-search comparisons with the

rest of the trajectory. We introduceCORE, a

fine search with context management. CORE
retrieves passages with a dense retriever. It

the narrowness of snippet-level evidence by

Deduplication.As the research
progresses, later sub-queries may retrieve snippets
that already appeared in earlier search observations,
and parallel sub-queries within a single search call
may return the same snippet. Because the first oc-
currence remains in the agent's context, showing
the same text again increases token cost without
adding new evidence. Context management there-
fore tracks the snippets already shown to the agent
and replaces any repeated occurrences with com-
pact references.

initially empty, containing the keys of all snippets
shown to the agent so far. For a search result e,

Closed-search benchmarks.We evaluate on
three benchmarks. The first is the standard
BrowseComp-Plus (Chen et al., 2026c), which has
830 questions over a fixed corpus of 100K web
documents. The other two are more challenging be-
cause their corpora are much larger: BrowseComp-
Wikipedia (Yang et al., 2026) has 232 questions
over 6M Wikipedia articles, and BrowseComp-
PlusCM (Sharifymoghaddam et al., 2026) has 57
questions over 553M ClimbMix documents. More
details of these benchmarks are presented in Ap-
pendix A.1.
Harnesses.We compare CORE with two re-
cent state-of-the-art open-source harnesses: Tongyi
DeepResearch (Tongyi DeepResearch Team et al.,
2025) and OpenResearcher (Li et al., 2026b).

main harness comparison: GPT-5.4 (high reason-
ing effort), Qwen3.8-27B (Qwen Team, 2026), and

evidence.excerpt:
Our experiments examine multi-step information
seeking on three benchmarks with fixed text col-
lections and reference answers. We chose this set-
ting on purpose because it allows controlled, re-
producible comparisons across harnesses. Fixed
corpora do not capture the dynamic and hetero-
geneous nature of the open web, and reference-
answer-based evaluation may not fully reflect the
quality of long-form synthesis in less constrained
research tasks. Evaluating on live web search and
open-ended research reports is beyond the scope
of this work. We leave it to future research, which
could test whether our findings carry over beyond
fixed-corpus question answering.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evidence recall is an objective, judge-independent measurement derived from fixed benchmark relevance annotations, and it moves in the same direction as the LLM-judged accuracy gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Answer accuracy is established by a GPT-5.5 LLM judge against reference answers, while evidence recall is computed from fixed benchmark document-level relevance annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The CORE harness is training-free and heuristic: no model weights, prompts, or harness parameters are tuned against the benchmark outcomes, and the component analysis fixes shared inference settings, index, context budget, and judge across configurations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of superior answer accuracy, evidence recall, and context efficiency are well supported across corpora up to 553 million documents, with consistent gains shown in Table 1 and Table 2.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation conducts rigorous, controlled closed-search comparisons on three benchmarks (BrowseComp-Plus, BrowseComp-Wikipedia, and BrowseComp-PlusCM) across three agent models against established harnesses (Tongyi DeepResearch and OpenResearcher), supported by an ablation study.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Document-level evidence recall computed against fixed benchmark annotations provides an objective, judge-independent measurement alongside the LLM judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: GPT-5.5 LLM-as-a-judge accuracy based on reference answers, alongside ground-truth document-level evidence recall annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Training-free heuristic and architecture design; no model weights were tuned against the benchmark evaluations.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss the boundary conditions, notably that the empirical findings are evaluated on closed-search benchmarks with static corpora and reference answers, leaving open-ended live web browsing to future work.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed: coarse candidate passage retrieval uses dense embeddings, followed by late-interaction MaxSim passage reranking and segment scoring without extra encoding, accompanied by goal-directed context expansion and snippet-level hash deduplication.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a clear, reproducible, training-free architectural advance for deep research harnesses with thorough benchmarking across multiple scales and models, complete baseline controls, and explicit ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces CORE, a training-free deep research harness that integrates coarse-to-fine passage retrieval and snippet extraction via reused late-interaction ColBERT similarities, coupled with context management (context expansion and cross-search deduplication).

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a clear, reproducible, training-free architectural advance for deep research harnesses with thorough benchmarking across multiple scales and models, complete baseline controls, and explicit ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently discuss the boundary conditions, notably that the empirical findings are evaluated on closed-search benchmarks with static corpora and reference answers, leaving open-ended live web browsing to future work.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
